text:
Making the patient sit upright at 90° is not necessary — the JVP is best examined with the patient reclined at 30–45°, since upright positioning can collapse the vein and obscure the pulse. Good lighting, tangential viewing, and assessing waveform/height relative to the sternal angle are all needed. The shared note is incorrect: tense neck muscles can obscure the JVP, so relaxation is relevant.
CONFIDENCE: 85
